reigns.note: Eponymous hero — son of Poseidon by a nymph of the Italian country; Pausanias says both the city and its river were called after him. Local naming tradition, not a civic king or successor in a royal line.

Spartan oecist of the Lacedaemonian colony — Delphi promised him territory when rain fell under a cloudless sky (aethra); his wife Aethra's tears solved the riddle, and that night he took Tarentum from the barbarians. Before Italy a dolphin brought him ashore after shipwreck in the Crisaean sea (Delphi offering with Taras). Founder, not the head of a padded king-list. Ovid later calls the place Spartan Tarentum (Met. 15.1–91) without naming him. Distinguishes from Arcadian Phalanthus son of Agelaus (Paus. 8.35.9).
